title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 15

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When does the incident-reporting session start?
tasks.audioText: The safety and engineering tutor will review incident communication on Friday at ten fifteen. Students should bring the incident-report template. The lesson will distinguish an observation, an immediate action and a later investigation finding.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which reporting template is required?
tasks.audioText: The safety and engineering tutor will review incident communication on Friday at ten fifteen. Students should bring the incident-report template. The lesson will distinguish an observation, an immediate action and a later investigation finding.

tasks.prompt: An engineering incident report records facts in a clear sequence. It may include time and location, people or equipment involved, the observed event and immediate action. A later investigation may identify causes, but these should not be presented as established facts before the investigation is complete. Reports should follow the approved process and protect confidential information. Reading 1. What information may an incident report include?
options: Purchase price, supplier address and delivery date
Only the name of the person who submitted the report
Time, location, people or equipment involved, observed event and immediate action
A final diagnosis even when the investigation is incomplete

tasks.prompt: How should findings from an incomplete investigation be described?
options: They should be presented as confirmed conclusions
They should replace the original observations
They should be removed from the report
They should not be presented as established facts

tasks.prompt: The immediate action ___ in the incident report.
Which TWO details belong in the factual, initial stage of an engineering incident report?
A formal written account of an event is an incident ___.
A fault has been reported, but its cause has not been confirmed. How should the report describe it?
options: The cause has not yet been established; record the observed condition and actions taken, and state that the investigation is continuing.
Record the suspected cause as confirmed so the report can be closed.
Leave the cause field blank and omit the unresolved fault from the handover.
Copy the cause from an earlier report if the symptoms look similar.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of engineering incident communication in a logical order.
options: Add verified investigation findings when available
Submit the report through the approved route
Record the time, place and observed event
correctOrder: Record the time, place and observed event
Submit the report through the approved route
Add verified investigation findings when available

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how to communicate an engineering incident accurately. Distinguish observed facts, immediate actions and later findings.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the report distinguishes observed facts from immediate actions and later findings (0–2); it explains why causes should remain unconfirmed until supported by investigation evidence (0–2); the report is factual, clearly sequenced and grammatically understandable (0–2); incident-reporting vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
